title: Option: absence as a type
summary: Maybe-a-value is Option<T> — the compiler forces every caller to face the None case.
lecture: Rust has no null. A value that might not exist is Option<T>: Some(value) or None. The absence is part of the type, so forgetting to handle it is a compile error, not a 3am page.

Signatures speak: `fn first_char(s: &str) -> char` promises a char ALWAYS — a lie for the empty string that unwrap() converts into a runtime panic. `-> Option<char>` tells the truth and hands the decision to the caller, who has context you don't.

.unwrap() is a claim that None is impossible right here. In puzzle terms: every unwrap you write is a place where a test with the right input can make your program die. Prefer returning the Option, or ?, or unwrap_or/map when a default genuinely exists.

example.caption: The iterator already speaks Option — don't unwrap it into a lie.
